title: Gravitational constant from information geometry
html:
Definition. Gravitational constant from information geometry

Definition. The gravitational constant G_q normalises the q-Yang--Mills--Levi variation (q-YM-Levi). It sets the ratio of curvature to stress-energy in the field equation \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\varTheta} = T^{(q)} (GR substrate geometry):

  G_q := \frac{c_q^3 \cdot \hbar_q}{S_{\mathrm{cell}}(q)}
  = \frac{c_q^3 \cdot (2q - 1)}{q^2 \cdot \eta_q \cdot \hbar_q},

where c_q = 1/(q-1) is the speed of light (speed of light), \hbar_q = (q-1)/q, \eta_q = (2q-1)/q^3 is the operational entropy (operational entropy), and S_{\mathrm{cell}}(q) = (q-1)^2/q^3 is the cumulative jet-tower entropy of a Planck cell. In Planck units, G_{\mathrm{Planck}} = G_q\,(\hbar_q/c_q)^2 = 1 identically for all q > 1.
